app.name: Zoom General app (Zoom App Marketplace)
app.category: Zoom Workplace / App Marketplace, General app

verdict.summary: Connecting your own Zoom account through your own General app is quick and needs no review. Making the app available to other users outside your Zoom account means passing Marketplace functional and security review, which covers every requested scope and needs a test plan, technical design and domain-verified documents.
verdict.hands_on_effort: About 1-2 hours for the own-account setup. Several days of work for a public submission package, plus the review wait.
verdict.time_to_first_connection: Under 1 hour once the developer role is confirmed (estimate, not from sources).
verdict.approval_wait: None for your own account or same-organization users. Public review: community forum reports of 4+ weeks end to end; Zoom's stated SLA is unclear (see open questions).

gates.name: Development credentials, your own account
gates.unlocks: Create the General app, add scopes, and connect your own Zoom account using your own client ID and secret. Development-mode apps are limited to user accounts in the same Zoom org as the app.
limits: Development mode is restricted to user accounts in the same Zoom org (community-reported).
Your account must be the account owner, an account admin, or hold the Zoom for developers role.
Adding a scope submits a request to the Zoom Security Review team, which may reject it.
gates.time_to_reach: Minutes to about 1 hour, once you have the developer role.

gates.name: Private or beta app (invited/internal users)
gates.unlocks: Users in your own Zoom account can install the app without the standard Marketplace review. Private and beta apps do not require review. An account admin or a user with Marketplace permissions must pre-approve the app for the account before end users can enable it.
limits: Beta and private apps skip review, but the docs in this research do not state a user or install cap for them (open question).
Unlisted apps are a different path: they need review and full listing metadata, and are distributed by authorization URL.
Install can fail for users without install privileges; the account owner may need to change admin role settings (community-reported).
gates.time_to_reach: No Zoom review wait. Admin pre-approval time depends on your account.

gates.name: Public Marketplace listing (anyone)
gates.unlocks: Any Zoom user can install the app from the Marketplace. Requires functional review, security review, and domain-verified listing documents.
limits: Review checks OWASP Top 10 risks, least-privilege scopes, and a Technical Design section.
Production client ID is used for first-time submissions.
Any scope change after publishing repeats both functional and security review.
Free-account developers must upgrade to Free with Credit Card or submit an entity-information form.
gates.time_to_reach: Weeks. Community reports 4+ weeks for the full publishing process; the security review can take up to 2 weeks after functional review. Current SLA unverified.

steps.title: Confirm you can create a General app
steps.detail: Sign in to marketplace.zoom.us with an account that is the account owner, an account admin, or has the Zoom for developers role. If the Developer link does not appear, an admin must enable the role.
gotchas: The Developer link only shows for users with developer permissions.
Admin path: User Management > Roles > Role Settings > Advanced features, then select View and Edit for Zoom for developers.

steps.title: Decide managed Composio auth or your own app
steps.detail: Composio offers managed OAuth for Zoom, so you can start there. Register your own General app only if you need your own consent-screen brand, scopes beyond Composio's default list, or control over the redirect URI and submission.
gotchas: Composio's default scope set has 26 granular scopes; a custom app needs every scope you use added in its own build flow.

steps.title: Create the General app
steps.detail: On marketplace.zoom.us, open Develop, choose Build an app, select General app and click Create. Name the app and continue to the Basic Info page.
gotchas: Only apps made through the build flow get granular scopes.

steps.title: Choose the app management type
steps.detail: On Basic Info, choose admin-managed or user-managed. This choice changes which features and scopes are available, so decide before you add scopes.
gotchas: Admin-managed apps can grant admin capabilities only to an account admin or owner.

steps.title: Copy the development client credentials
steps.detail: Open Basic Information > App Credentials and copy the development Client ID and Client Secret. Use development credentials for building and testing; production credentials are used for publishing.

values.label: Credentials used now
values.value: Development Client ID and Client Secret

gotchas: Public client IDs (no secret, PKCE) are a separate setting, and a published PKCE app needs a written reason for the public client.

steps.title: Set the OAuth redirect URL and allow list
steps.detail: In the OAuth Information section, set the OAuth Redirect URL and add the same URL to OAuth allow lists. The redirect_uri in the token exchange must match the Redirect URL exactly. Strict mode is optional but checks the URL character by character.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

values.label: Allow list
values.value: Same Composio callback URL (full URL or base URL without path)

gotchas: Do not use loopback (127.0.0.1) or development URLs for production; Zoom says they may be rejected in review.
Loopback is only for PKCE or native clients, not simple confidential apps.
Composio's default redirect URI is listed two different ways; confirm the value in your Composio auth config before saving.

steps.title: Add only the scopes you need
steps.detail: In the build flow, add each scope your app calls, and set it as required or optional. Scope requests go to the Zoom Security Review team, and each scope needs a written justification. Remove any scope the app does not use, and avoid a broader scope when a narrower one covers the same call.
gotchas: Scopes must be added in the build flow before the authorization page can request them.
Redundant scopes are rejected: view-only meeting scopes are redundant when View and manage user meetings is also requested.
Unjustified scopes are denied and removed.

steps.title: Draft scope justifications and test notes
steps.detail: An agent can draft one justification per scope from your code, mapping each scope to the API call that uses it. Review these with the developer before entering them in the build flow. Include test instructions for each scope.
gotchas: Zoom denies scopes that lack justification and detailed testing instructions.

steps.title: Connect your own account in Composio or your app
steps.detail: Authorize your own Zoom account through the app to confirm the flow. Access tokens last one hour, so check that refresh works. Refresh tokens last 90 days; use the latest refresh token returned on each refresh.
gotchas: If a refresh token expires, the user must restart authorization.
Revoke tokens by POSTing to https://zoom.us/oauth/revoke with Basic auth (Client ID and secret).

steps.title: Pre-approve the app for your account and test users
steps.detail: Have an account admin or a user with Marketplace permissions pre-approve the app so users in your account can enable it. Test installs with a non-admin user, since installs can fail without install privileges.
gotchas: Admin-managed apps grant admin capabilities only to account admins or owners.

steps.title: Prepare listing documents on owned domains
steps.detail: An agent can draft the privacy policy, terms of use, support page and user documentation. Host them on a company-owned fully qualified domain, not Google Drive or Dropbox. The support page needs hours and a first-response SLA; user docs must cover adding, using and removing the app.
gotchas: Verify domains for the privacy, terms, OAuth redirect, webhook and home URLs (TXT record, HTML file, meta tag, or support request).
Listing needs 2-3 images at 1200 x 780 px; one optional MP4 up to 40 MB; short description up to 150 characters.

steps.title: Add the deauthorization webhook
steps.detail: Build the notification endpoint Zoom calls when a user removes the app. On receipt, delete that user's data. An agent can implement the endpoint and deletion path, then the developer confirms it in the app settings.
gotchas: Zoom requires deletion of all associated user data on removal.

steps.title: Write the Technical Design and Security Review inputs
steps.detail: Complete the Technical Design section in the build flow. Describe architecture, security controls, and how data from each OAuth scope is used. The security review tests OWASP Top 10 risks, least-privilege checks, web scanning, misuse testing and vulnerable libraries.
gotchas: Load testing and DoS/DDoS are not part of the security review.

steps.title: Write the test plan and submit
steps.detail: Put the test plan in the Release Notes field with test credentials for each account role the app uses. Enter the production client ID during authorization for the first submission, then submit for review. Resubmissions also need a test plan.
gotchas: Wrong client ID and missing test plans are common rejection reasons.
Reviewers authorise with the production client ID (community-reported).

steps.title: Wait for review and respond to feedback
steps.detail: Zoom reviews functionality and security, then may return remediation feedback. Plan for weeks, not days, and respond to each requested scope or documentation change. Unverified forum reports show slower responses after an October 2026 update.
gotchas: Review time is longer for apps with many scopes and unclear test plans.
Changes to scope or data access repeat functional and security review.

requirements.item: Account role to create the app
requirements.detail: Account owner, account admin, or Zoom for developers role. Without it the Developer link does not appear; an admin can enable it under Role Settings > Advanced features.

requirements.item: OAuth redirect URL and allow list
requirements.detail: Set the Redirect URL and add it to the allow list. Use the Composio callback URL from your Composio auth config. The token exchange redirect_uri must match exactly.
Simple confidential OAuth apps must use HTTPS redirect URIs. Loopback is only for PKCE or native clients.
An account admin or a user with Marketplace permissions must pre-approve the app before end users can enable it.
Users inside your own Zoom account can install internal apps without standard Marketplace review. External users need the app to pass review.
Unlisted apps are distributed by authorization URL but still need full listing metadata and review.

requirements.item: Domain validation of documents and URLs
requirements.detail: Privacy, terms, OAuth redirect, webhook and home URLs must be validated: TXT record, HTML file, meta tag, or a manual support request.
Privacy, terms, support and documentation must be on company-owned domains. Google Drive and Dropbox are not permitted.

User docs cover adding, using and removing the app. The support page lists hours and a first-response SLA. Listing: 2-3 images at 1200 x 780 px; optional MP4 up to 40 MB; short description up to 150 characters.
Put the test plan in the Release Notes field with test credentials for each account role. Required for resubmissions too.

requirements.item: Production client ID for first submission
requirements.detail: Use the Production Client ID during authorization for first-time submissions. Development client ID is for update requests.
Describe architecture, security controls, and OAuth scope data use. Security testing covers OWASP Top 10, least privilege, web scanning and vulnerable libraries.
Production apps receive a notification when a user removes the app and must delete that user's data.

requirements.item: Paid or verified account for submission
requirements.detail: Free-account developers must upgrade to Free with Credit Card or submit the entity-information form.
Access tokens last 1 hour and refresh tokens 90 days. Use the latest refresh token on each refresh; expired refresh tokens require the user to restart authorization.

scopes.scope: Default Composio set (26 granular scopes), e.g. meeting:read:list_meetings, webinar:read:webinar, user:read:user
scopes.effect: Zoom's docs list no separate sensitive or restricted tier; every scope goes through the same Security Review and needs its own justification. Scopes must be added in the build flow before they can be requested.
A delete-action scope. Expect reviewers to ask why deletion is needed and to check it against least-privilege; drop it if the app only reads transcripts.

scopes.scope: Any scope duplicating a broader scope (e.g. view-only meeting scope alongside View and manage user meetings)
scopes.effect: Rejected as redundant. Request only the broadest scope you need.

scopes.scope: Admin-level capabilities (if your app is admin-managed)
scopes.effect: Only account admins or owners can grant admin capabilities, so end users without those roles cannot grant them.

blockers.symptom: Developer link missing in marketplace.zoom.us; cannot create the app.
blockers.fix: An account owner or admin enables Zoom for developers under User Management > Roles > Role Settings > Advanced features (View and Edit).

blockers.symptom: Other users cannot install or enable the unpublished app.
blockers.cause: Their admin role lacks install privileges, or the app is not pre-approved.
blockers.fix: Pre-approve the app for the account, and have the account owner check admin role settings for install privileges.

blockers.symptom: Submission rejected for redirect URI or loopback.
blockers.cause: Loopback or development URLs used in a production-facing app.
blockers.fix: Use an HTTPS redirect URI on a verified domain, matching the allow list exactly.

blockers.symptom: Submission rejected for test plan or client ID.
blockers.cause: Test plan missing details or the development client ID used for a first-time submission.
blockers.fix: Write a test plan with test credentials per role in Release Notes, and use the Production Client ID for the first submission.

blockers.symptom: Scopes denied or removed during review.
blockers.cause: Scopes lack justification or testing instructions, or they are redundant.
blockers.fix: Justify each scope, remove unused scopes, and drop narrower duplicates.

blockers.cause: Documents hosted on Google Drive or Dropbox, or domains not validated.
blockers.fix: Host on company-owned domains and complete domain validation before submitting.

blockers.symptom: App fails review for missing metadata or incomplete user documentation.
blockers.cause: Required listing fields or support SLA missing.
blockers.fix: Complete all listing fields, support hours and first-response SLA, and add-remove-use user docs.

blockers.symptom: App cannot be created after several attempts in one day.
blockers.cause: Forum-reported cap on apps created within 24 hours (old, unverified).
blockers.fix: Wait 24 hours and avoid repeat app creation; confirm current limits with Zoom support.

composio.note: Start on Composio managed OAuth to get going quickly. Move to your own Zoom General app when you need your own brand on the consent screen, scopes beyond the default 26, or control over the redirect URI and Marketplace submission. Your own app brings its own client ID/secret, redirect URI and allow list, and Marketplace review if you publish to external users.

evidence.claim: Composio's Zoom toolkit has managed OAuth available with OAUTH2 mode; authorize URL is zoom.us/oauth/authorize and token URL is zoom.us/oauth/token.
evidence.quote: managed_oauth_available: true; authorization_url: https://zoom.us/oauth/authorize; token_url: https://zoom.us/oauth/token

evidence.claim: Allow-list entries can be a full callback URL or a base URL with no path or query.
evidence.quote: A base URL without a path or query parameters (e.g., https://subdomain.domain.tld)

evidence.claim: Loopback and development redirect URLs are fine for development, but Zoom says to avoid them in production because they may be rejected during marketplace review.
evidence.quote: These resources are not suitable for production-ready end users and may be rejected during the marketplace publishing review.

evidence.claim: Strict mode checks the redirect URL character by character against the registered value, whether or not the subdomain check is also on.
evidence.quote: the redirect URL is verified character by character, regardless of whether the subdomain check is enabled.

evidence.claim: The token exchange POSTs to zoom.us/oauth/token with grant_type=authorization_code, and the redirect_uri must match the OAuth Redirect URL in the Marketplace app.
evidence.quote: Use the same OAuth Redirect URL in your Marketplace app.

evidence.claim: Access tokens for user authorization last one hour; the refresh token is returned alongside them and must be used to get a new access token.
evidence.quote: Access tokens expire after one hour. After your access token expires, you can follow the refresh flow to get a new one.

evidence.claim: Refresh tokens expire after 90 days, and each refresh should use the latest refresh token returned; when one expires, the user must restart the authorization flow.
evidence.quote: Refresh tokens expire after 90 days. You should always use the latest refresh token for the next refresh request.

evidence.claim: Access tokens can be revoked by POSTing to zoom.us/oauth/revoke with the token and the Client ID and secret in a Basic header.
evidence.quote: To revoke an access token, send a POST request to https://zoom.us/oauth/revoke with a basic authorization header.

evidence.claim: PKCE is supported for user authorization: a public client ID with no secret is used, code_challenge_method must be S256 for public clients, and the consent screen must always show.
evidence.quote: Public clients must use S256.

evidence.claim: A public client ID is turned on in the app's Basic Information > App Credentials with Use Public Client OAuth; if you publish a PKCE app, the review asks you to explain why a public client is needed.
evidence.quote: If you make your app public, you may need to add an explanation why your application requires a public client ID in production.

evidence.claim: Loopback redirect URIs (127.0.0.1 with any port, no localhost) are for PKCE-enabled or native clients only; simple confidential OAuth apps must use HTTPS redirect URIs.
evidence.quote: Do not use loopback for simple OAuth apps that are not PKCE-enabled and native apps.

evidence.claim: Composio's default Zoom scope set contains 26 granular scopes spanning meetings, webinars, cloud recordings, archiving, contacts and user settings.
evidence.quote: meeting:read:list_meetings, meeting:write:meeting, webinar:read:webinar, cloud_recording:read:meeting_transcript, user:read:user

evidence.claim: Zoom's deauthorization webhook is sent to a notification endpoint for production apps when a user removes the app, and the app must then delete that user's data.
evidence.quote: apps must delete all associated user data.

evidence.claim: Granular scopes are the default for newly created apps, and the classic scopes (user-level, admin-level, Master-level) apply to older apps.
evidence.quote: Newly created apps use granular scopes, including new apps created using the new build flow

evidence.claim: Granular scopes follow service:action:data_claim:access, with four actions (read, write, update, delete) and an access level that is empty, admin, or master.
evidence.quote: There are total of 4 actions in granular scopes: read, write, update and delete.

evidence.claim: Granular scopes are only available to apps built through the Marketplace app creation build flow; classic-scope apps cannot see them.
evidence.quote: Granular and optional scopes are only available for new apps created using the Zoom Marketplace app creation build flow.

evidence.claim: Admin-managed apps can grant admin capabilities only to a user who is an account admin or owner; master-level scopes can only be granted to account-level apps by account owners.
evidence.quote: The user adding the app must be an account admin or owner in order to be granted admin capabilities.

evidence.claim: Required and optional scopes can be set in the build flow; the basic authorization query uses those defaults, and the advanced query can override which scopes are required or optional for a given attempt.
evidence.quote: Basic authorization query uses the default required and optional scopes set by the developer in the build flow.

evidence.claim: Zoom's authorization page takes scope and optional_scope parameters; the scopes must already be added to the app in the build flow.
evidence.quote: Note that the scopes must have already been added to the app in the build flow.

evidence.claim: To enable apps for end-users, an account admin or a user with Marketplace permissions must pre-approve the app for the account.
evidence.quote: To enable apps for end-users, an account admin, or user with Marketplace permissions for their Zoom Account, must pre-approve the app.

evidence.claim: Adding a scope in the build flow submits a request to the Zoom Security Review team; reviewers may reject a scope they judge unnecessary, and each scope needs a description explaining why it is needed.
evidence.quote: If the Zoom Security Review team determines the requested scope is not necessary for your app, they may reject the scope request.

evidence.claim: Zoom's review checks that the app requests only the minimum necessary OAuth scopes; developers may be asked to remove unused or inappropriate scopes.
evidence.quote: Developers may be asked to remove unused or inappropriate scopes.

evidence.claim: Creating a General OAuth app requires an account whose user is the account owner, an account admin, or has the Zoom for developers role.
evidence.quote: You are either the Zoom account owner, account admin, or have been assigned the Zoom for developers role.

evidence.claim: Without justification and detailed testing instructions for each requested scope, Zoom denies the rest and requests the scope's removal.
evidence.quote: Without them, we deny the rest and request the removal of the scope.

evidence.claim: Zoom's docs contain no separate list of sensitive or restricted scopes with a different review track; every scope goes through the same Security Review.
Public and unlisted apps go through a dedicated review that either approves the app or gives remediation feedback; private and beta apps do not need review.
evidence.quote: Private and beta apps do not require review.

evidence.claim: The review has four parts: submission completeness and branding, functionality and compliance, a security review, and remediation when an app does not pass.
evidence.quote: The Zoom App Marketplace Security Review is designed to help protect customer data

evidence.claim: The security review tests against OWASP Top 10 risks, including least-privilege checks, web application scanning, manual misuse testing and vulnerable-library checks.
evidence.quote: Apps are tested against the OWASP Top 10 risks and undergo a variety of assessments

evidence.claim: The security review requires a Technical Design section in the build flow that describes architecture, security controls, and how data from OAuth scopes is used.
evidence.quote: The information you provide outlines how the app is built, what security controls are in place

evidence.claim: Load testing and DoS/DDoS simulations are not part of the security review.
evidence.quote: Load testing or DoS/DDoS simulations are not part of security review.

evidence.claim: Zoom's blog, fetched in this session, says apps are reviewed first come first serve, Monday to Friday, and that the submission response time is within 5 business days. The post is dated 2022, so it may be out of date.
evidence.quote: The app review submission response time is within 5 business days.

evidence.claim: A search snippet of the same blog quoted a 72-hour first-response SLA with typical response in 36 hours; the fetched page did not show that wording, so the two versions conflict and the current SLA is unclear.
evidence.quote: We have a 72 hour first response SLA, and typically respond within 36 hours of your submission.

evidence.claim: Review time depends on app quality, how many features and scopes there are, and how clear the descriptions, images and videos are; apps with defined scopes and a clear test plan are tested fastest.
evidence.quote: Testing time is typically the shortest for apps that have properly defined scopes, a clear test plan

evidence.claim: The Marketplace shows the Developer link only to users with developer permissions, so a user who lacks it has to get that permission from an admin.
evidence.quote: The Marketplace only displays the Developer link when it detects that the user has the proper developer permissions.

evidence.claim: Developers on the Zoom developer forum report full-process timelines of several weeks, and the security review can take up to two weeks after functional review.
evidence.quote: After you complete the functional review, the security review can take up to 2 weeks

evidence.claim: A July 2026 forum post reports a publishing process of 4+ weeks and a functional review with no reply after 72 hours.
evidence.quote: the full publishing process can take 4+ weeks

evidence.claim: An October 24, 2026 forum announcement is titled as an update to app review submission response time due to increased submission volume; the post body was not readable, so the current timeline is unverified.
evidence.quote: due to increased submission volume, we’re updating our app review Submission Resp

evidence.claim: Submission requires domain validation of the Privacy Policy, Terms of Use, OAuth redirect, webhook and home URLs; the four methods are a TXT record, an HTML file, a meta tag, or a manual request to Zoom support.
evidence.quote: Request manual approval from Zoom support. This is a good option to choose if you do not have permission

evidence.claim: Production client ID is used for first-time submissions; development client ID is used for update requests.
evidence.quote: For First-time submissions Make sure your environment is using the Production Client ID during authorization.

evidence.claim: A test plan is required for every submission, including resubmissions; put it in the Release Notes field, with test credentials for each account role the app uses.
evidence.quote: A test plan is required for each submission, including re-submissions.

evidence.claim: Privacy, terms, support and documentation URLs must be on company-owned fully qualified domains; Google Drive and Dropbox hosting is not permitted.
evidence.quote: Hosting these documents on third-party platforms like Google Drive or Dropbox is not permitted.

evidence.claim: User documentation must cover adding, using and removing the app; the support page must give hours and a first-response SLA.
evidence.quote: Your support page should include: Support team's hours of operation. First Response SLA

evidence.claim: Listing assets: 2 to 3 images at 1200 x 780 px in JPG, GIF, JPEG or PNG; optional one MP4 video up to 40 MB. Short description is limited to 150 characters.
evidence.quote: Video: Upload up to 1 video, maximum size 40 MB

evidence.claim: Free-account developers must upgrade to Free with Credit Card or submit an entity-information form to satisfy U.S. government compliance rules.
evidence.quote: Upgrade your account to Free with Credit Card.

evidence.claim: An admin enables the role by going to User Management > Roles > Role Settings > Advanced features and selecting View and Edit for Zoom for developers.
evidence.quote: select the View and Edit checkboxes for Zoom for developers.

evidence.claim: Unlisted apps still need full listing metadata; the app fails review if required metadata is missing, and unlisted apps are distributed by authorization URL.
evidence.quote: The app will fail the review process if the required metadata is missing.

evidence.claim: Users inside the developer's own Zoom account can install an app without the standard Marketplace review; external-audience apps must pass review before users can install them.
evidence.quote: These apps are intended for internal use and don't require the standard Marketplace review.

evidence.claim: A developer-community answer says apps in development mode are limited to user accounts in the same Zoom org, and external test users need production or beta approval.
evidence.quote: Zoom apps are limited to user accounts in the same Zoom org as the app while in development mode.

evidence.claim: Changing scopes on a published app requires both functional and security review; new scopes need a test plan and must be tested with development credentials on update requests.
evidence.quote: Changes to scope, features, or data access need to go through both a functional and a security review

evidence.claim: Common rejection reasons include a test plan with insufficient information, wrong client ID, third-party-hosted documents, incomplete user documentation, unjustified or redundant scopes, and the wrong Add-app option.
evidence.quote: Common reasons for app submission rejection - test plan, client ID, documentation standards, scope management

evidence.claim: Zoom's docs say a redundant scope is rejected: an app requesting both the view and the view-and-manage user meetings scopes is told the view-only one is redundant.
evidence.quote: the latter is redundant. All view-related API calls can be handled with the View and manage user meetings scope.

evidence.claim: A developer-forum thread reports a limit on how many OAuth apps can be created, which a Zoom team member described as a cap on apps created within 24 hours. The thread is old and unverified against current docs.
evidence.quote: Turns out we only limit the maximum number of apps created within a 24 hour period.

evidence.claim: No install cap or user limit for unreviewed or unlisted OAuth apps was found in the official docs or changelog; the only documented gate for unreviewed apps is the development-mode same-organization restriction.
To start, sign in at the Zoom App Marketplace, open Developer, go to Created apps, choose Develop then Build an app, select General app and click Create.
evidence.quote: On the Created apps page, click Develop and select Build an app.

evidence.claim: marketplace.zoom.us returned HTTP 200 with no login wall on a public probe; the app build pages behind it need a signed-in developer-permissioned account.
evidence.quote: status 200; title: App Marketplace; login_wall: false

evidence.claim: Probing Zoom's authorize endpoint with an invalid client ID returned error code 4702 'Invalid client_id' after redirecting to the sign-in page, which confirms the endpoint is live and validates client IDs.
evidence.quote: {"status":false,"errorCode":4702,"errorMessage":"Invalid client_id: oauth-runway-probe-invalid-client"}

evidence.claim: A third-party developer blog says reviewers authorize with the production client ID, and they swapped in production credentials and checked the redirect URI before submitting.
evidence.quote: Reviewers authorise with the Production client ID.

evidence.claim: A developer-forum answer says an unpublished app may fail to install for a user without install privileges, and that the account owner may need to change the admin role settings.
evidence.quote: It could be that your particular Admin role settings do not allow for app install privileges.

evidence.claim: On Basic Info, the builder asks you to choose admin-managed or user-managed, and that choice changes which features and scopes are available.
evidence.quote: The app management type affects the features and scopes available to your app.

evidence.claim: The build flow generates separate development and production client credentials; development credentials are for building and testing, production credentials for publishing.
evidence.quote: Use production credentials once you are ready to publish your app on the Marketplace.

evidence.claim: The OAuth Information section requires an OAuth redirect URL and OAuth allow lists; strict mode and subdomain check are optional.
evidence.quote: OAuth allow lists (required): Add any unique URLs that Zoom should allow as valid redirects

open_questions: Review SLA is unclear: a 2022 blog says submission response within 5 business days, a search snippet quotes a 72-hour first-response SLA, and an October 2026 forum post about changed response times could not be read. Treat all timelines as unverified.
No published list of sensitive or restricted Zoom scopes with a separate review path was found. Only the general Security Review and per-scope justification were confirmed.
No install cap or user limit for private, beta, or unlisted apps was found. The only cap found is a forum-reported 24-hour app-creation limit, which is old and unverified.

Composio's default redirect URI differs between sources: the toolkit record shows https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add, and a probe used https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback. Confirm the exact value in your Composio auth config before entering it in the Zoom allow list.
Business verification, paid-plan or partner-program requirements were not found beyond the free-account credit-card or entity-form rule.
Developer build pages sit behind login, so UI labels come from the docs, not the live portal. The Priority Review process exists per the docs, but its details could not be read.
Refresh token rotation details beyond using the latest refresh token and the 90-day expiry were not confirmed for the user-authorization flow.
Whether Composio's managed app uses PKCE or a client secret was not confirmed.
